text:
maria: quick follow-up to the RFC — proposing an explicit atomic shard-swap + rollback protocol for safetensors shards. saw a few flakes in canary where half the shard set landed and inference errored.
liam: can you sketch the flow? is this overlay staging like we do for kernel upgrades?
maria: yes, two-phase. Stage full shard set into ephemeral overlay dir, verify checksums, run lightweight sanity inference, then atomically switch a symlink/manifest pointer. If verification fails we drop overlay. keeps live root always consistent.
akshay: what about memory pressure? staging full model means double RAM/disk for a bit.
maria: agreed. tradeoffs: for large models we do "streamed stage" + quick integrity checks per-shard (sha256) and a final manifest hash. We only keep minimal in-memory metadata until switch. Disk still needs enough headroom.
sophie: how does this interact with warmup (kv cache) and active requests? we can't just drop caches.
maria: plan: at switch time we mark old KV-cache entries as retired and start populating new cache entries incrementally. active inference continues pinned to old version until completion (routing layer tiebreaker by request id). New requests route to new version after switch. avoids mid-request model mismatch.
liam: routing layer changes required — pointer swap must be linearizable.
maria: yep. implement via single-writer manifest update + lease. clients read manifest atomically. we already have a manifest object for Dedicated; reuse that mechanism.
akshay: rollback: suppose a shard mismatches checksum after switch (corrupt object store), how do we recover?
maria: immediate rollback: manifest swap back to previous pointer. If overlay failed earlier, nothing changed. If corruption detected post-switch during background validation we trigger auto-rollback and schedule a degraded-mode route (read-only or smaller variant) and alert.
reloader-bot: action required: deploy reloader that supports staged overlays, final manifest swap, and a /force-rollback admin endpoint.
sophie: testing? need chaos tests: partial upload, truncated shard, slow object store, and kv-cache drift.
maria: agreed. test plan: unit tests for manifest checksums, e2e with s3 simulator (inject corrupt objects), canary on single shard models, then scale to 8/16-shard. add perf benchmark for staging overhead.
liam: UX: operators need clear telemetry — show staging progress, verified shards, current vs pending manifest, rollback reason.
akshay: one nit: safetensors header doesn't have an integrity block. proposal: embed a small json metadata sidecar (.meta) per shard with: {"sha256":"...","size":"...","cipher":"none"}. add optional encryption field for future.
maria: yep included in RFC follow-up. small example:
```
{
  "shard_index": 2,
  "sha256": "b4c3...",
  "size": 234567890,
  "version": 1
}
```
liam: sounds good. any perf hit from computing sha256? parallelize checks across cores, and skip when objectstore provides etag-style digest.
sophie: +1. also ensure metrics for stage-time and rollback-rate.
maria: OK I'll update the RFC doc with the state machine, admin endpoints, and test matrix. action items: maria -> PR for reloader, liam -> routing linearizability spec, akshay -> disk/memory headroom limits, sophie -> chaos test scenarios. tagging follow-up in eng-ml agenda. :rocket:
